claims.text: The starting ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder has a BCC solid-solution structure.
The starting powder contains nanoscale grains.
High-energy milling may introduce oxygen contamination into the powder.
SPS at 850-950 °C provides an optimum balance between diffusion activity and secondary-phase precipitation.
SPS is proposed under vacuum or argon at 50-100 MPa for 5-10 minutes.
At 850-950 °C, enhanced diffusion of Ti and V promotes secondary-phase nucleation.
Fine, coherent Mg2Ti and Mg2V Laves-phase precipitates form at grain boundaries.
Fine, coherent B2-ordered FeCo precipitates form at grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary precipitates impede Mg diffusion and thereby retard Mg volatilization.
The precipitates block oxygen diffusion paths and reduce oxygen ingress.
The precipitates pin grain boundaries and increase hardness.
Secondary-phase precipitation enhances densification.
The proposed SPS window produces greater than 95% relative density.
The proposed SPS window increases hardness by 30-50% compared with the stated as-sintered reference.
The proposed SPS window forms a stable protective oxide layer rich in Al2O3 and TiO2.
The protective layer reduces oxidation kinetics.
Below 800 °C, insufficient diffusion prevents secondary-phase barrier formation and leaves the material porous and under-densified.
Above 1000 °C, Mg volatilization causes composition deviation.
Composition deviation above 1000 °C promotes brittle intermetallic phases and compromises barrier integrity.
The mechanism fails below 800 °C or above 1000 °C.

contradictions.description: The predicted 30-50% hardness increase is defined relative to an 'as-sintered state,' although the intervention itself is SPS; the reference state is therefore ambiguous and may be the same state as the predicted outcome.

The mechanism attributes secondary-phase precipitation specifically to Ti and V diffusion, but the structural mediator also includes B2 FeCo precipitation without explaining how Ti/V diffusion causes that chemically distinct phase to form.
